master.title: BANGLADESH: Daily Press Review (20 Sept. 2023)
master.content:
The Delegation of the European Union to Bangladesh

Produced by Political, Trade, Press and Information Section

 

 

Dhaka had better address Europe s concerns (The Daily Star): Experts say European Parliament s resolution on rights issues a credible threat to exports; The European Parliament resolution on rights issues in Bangladesh adopted last Thursday is a warning for Dhaka before the EU takes actions that will hurt Bangladesh, said economists and international relations analysts. They said Europe's concerns over human rights, democracy and civic rights are not new, but they now align with the US's. Analysts said instead of ignoring and confronting them, Bangladesh should strengthen its engagement with the EU and address the genuine concerns that the EU has.

 

Bangladesh, Germany sign agreement to improve tannery working conditions (The Business Standard):  The People's Republic of Bangladesh and the Federal Republic of Germany have reaffirmed their dedication to environmental conservation and the enhancement of working conditions within the tannery industry by formalising two substantial technical cooperation agreements. The agreements, titled 'Integrated Management of the Sundarbans Mangroves and the Marine Protected Area "Swatch of No Ground (SoNG)"' and 'Good Working Conditions in Tanneries (GOTAN),' were formally signed on Tuesday (19 September). Economic Relations Division Secretary Sharifa Khan and Andreas Kuck, country director of GIZ on behalf of the Federal Republic of Germany in Bangladesh, signed the agreements on behalf of the two governments.

 

US seeks cooperation with Bangladesh on development, democracy (Dhaka Tribune): Counsellor of the US Department of State Derek Chollet has met Foreign Minister Dr AK Abdul Momen on the sidelines of UNGA78. We discussed our cooperation on economic development and climate change and the importance of protecting freedom of expression and democracy, Chollet tweeted after the meeting. Derek Chollet, before his visit to Bangladesh in February this year, said they see huge potential in their relationship with Bangladesh and there is a lot of room to grow.

 

US stresses fair polls, freedom of expression in Bangladesh (The New Age):  Washington has once again called on Dhaka to ensure that the upcoming general election is held in a free and fair manner and stressed the importance of protecting freedom of expression. The issues of democracy, free and fair elections and freedom of expression were discussed in separate bilateral talks held in New York on Monday on the sidelines of the 78th United Nations General Assembly. Bangladesh foreign minister AK Abdul Momen met with the US Department of State counsellor Derek Chollet  while another meeting was held between the US under-secretary for civilian security, democracy, and human rights, Uzra Zeya, and  Bangladesh foreign secretary Masud Bin Momen.

 

US wanted to know about Shahidul murder case (The Daily Star): A delegation of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) yesterday wanted to know from the BGMEA leaders about the progress in the labour leader Shahidul Islam murder case and the labour rights situation in the garment sector. The delegation enquired about the issues at a meeting with the leaders of Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association at its headquarters in the capital's Uttara, the association said in a statement. Shahid, president of the Gazipur unit of Bangladesh Garments and Industrial Workers Federation, was beaten to death outside Prince Jacquard Sweater Ltd in Tongi on the night of June 25.

 

Judges, magistrates concerned by European Parliament resolution on Bangladesh human rights (Dhaka Tribune): Bangladesh Judicial Service Association,  a professional body of judges and magistrates, have expressed concern about the European Parliament s recent resolution on the human rights situation in Bangladesh, notably the case of Odhikar. The resolution was an attempt to interfere with the judicial proceedings of an independent sovereign country, which was both unwanted and unwarranted, the association said in a press statement on Tuesday. Adilur Rahman Khan, secretary of the human rights organization, and ASM Nasiruddin Elan, its director, were recently sentenced to two years in prison in a case filed under the Information and Communication Technology Act for spreading false and fabricated news.

 

Conviction of Odhikar officials: Pro-BNP lawyers condemn BJSA statement on EP resolution (The Daily Star): Bangladesh Jatiotabadi Ainjibi Forum, a body of pro-BNP lawyers, today condemned the statement of Bangladesh Judicial Service Association that has expressed concern about the European Parliament (EP) resolution on the human rights situation in Bangladesh, particularly in the case of Odhikar's Secretary Adilur Rahman Khan and Director ASM Nasiruddin Elan. BJAF Secretary General Kayser Kamal issued a statement to this effect today also asking the authorities concerned to take steps against them (BJSA). In the statement, he said it is clearly shown from the statement made by BJSA that the judiciary has been fully politicised by the current regime.

 

Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council condemns support for Adlilur (Dhaka Tribune): The Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council has strongly condemned the support for Adilur Rahman from various global bodies following his and his associate s two-year conviction in a disinformation case. We are deeply shocked and appalled by the outpouring of support from different global bodies, including a resolution by the European Parliament, regarding the two-year conviction of Adilur Rahman and one of his associates. Both of them were found guilty of manufacturing and packaging an alarming scale of disinformation and outright lies through a report ostensibly to serve the agenda of radical religious forces, Hefazat-e-Islam, says the statement issued on Tuesday. On May 5, 2013, Hefazat, in collaboration with Jamaat-e-Islami, organized a rally in Dhaka, assembling thousands of madrasa students, where communal and radical demands were raised, including the enactment of a Taliban-style Shariah Law. The mob attacked public properties and business institutions, vandalized a political party office, and created havoc among the general populace. Law enforcement agencies took necessary steps to disperse the mob.

 

Protest rally demands release of Adilur, Elan (The New Age):  The families of the victims of enforced disappearance told a protest rally in Dhaka on Tuesday that none but Odhikar and its leadership Adilur Rahman and his colleague ASM Nasiruddin Elan stood by them and raised their voices locally and globally. None of the rights groups stood with us. It was only Odhikar who stood with us, Nasrin Jahan Smrity, wife of missing Mirpur-based trader Ismail Hossain, told a rally organised under the banner of Student-People against the Oppression on Tuesday in front of the National Museum in Dhaka. Nasrin blamed the Rapid Action Battalion for the disappearance of her husband from the capital s Mirpur on June 19, 2019, an allegation that the law-enforcing agency denied.

 

Yunus sued in Rangpur (The Daily Star): A case was filed against nobel laureate Dr Muhammad Yunus, founding chairman of Grameen Krishi (Agriculture) Foundation, and five others with Rangpur Labour Court yesterday.  The other accused are Nurjahan Begum, chairperson of board of directors of Grameen Krishi Foundation, Shamsud Doha, its acting managing director, and board members Imamus Sultan, Ratan Kumar Nag, and Shahjahan. Farukul Islam, senior farm manager (retired) of Grameen Krishi Foundation, filed the case, said Shamim Al Mamun, a lawyer for the complainant.

 

Child domestic workers in Bangladesh often work 15 hours a day: study (The New Age): Child domestic workers in Bangladesh work up to 20 hours a day, revealed a study released on Tuesday, reflecting conditions prevailing in a sector employing about two million people. The study was released by the Washington-based non-profit organisation Solidarity Centre, Bangladesh in the morning. Child domestic workers often work nearly 15 and a half hours daily, said the study conducted by Habibur Rahman, who teaches sociology and social work at the People s University of Bangladesh. The actual number of domestic workers is unknown but different organisations assume it to be about two million.

 

Over 100 Rohingyas detained for fleeing camps (The Daily Star): Police yesterday detained 101 Rohingyas for fleeing the refugee camps in Ukhiya upazila of Cox's Bazar. They were held near Ukhiya Degree College next to the Cox's Bazar-Teknaf highway between 11:00am and 1:00pm, said Sheikh Mohammad Ali, officer-in-charge of Ukhiya Police Station. Police have started strict surveillance to prevent the refugees from fleeing the camps. "Many Rohingyas leave camps dodging security personnel. Later, at a convenient time, they attempt to trespass into foreign territory. The police have started a special drive since September 16 to prevent that from happening," the OC added.

 

Mirza Abbas: Govt will not be allowed to hold stage-managed election anymore (Dhaka Tribune): BNP Standing Committee member Mirza Abbas on Tuesday urged the party activists to stay united as the Awami League government will not be allowed to hold another staged election. People do not want to see Awami League in power anymore. This time people will resist them, he said. Still there is time, dissolve parliament, resign after forming a caretaker government. We want a fair election, he said while addressing a public rally held in front of Zinzira BNP office in Keraniganj.

 

Where and when: A look into the upcoming AL and BNP rallies (The Business Standard): Although the venues of the events are set apart, the tension is thick, especially in the fallout of the BNP s countrywide road march on 18 July, which left one dead and scores injured. The BNP today (19 September) held the first of its 11 rallies slated for the next 15 days. Four days after, the Awami League will also kick start its own set of programmes. Although the venues of the events are set apart, the tension is thick, especially in the fallout of the BNP's countrywide road march on 18 July, which left one dead and scores injured. This was met with further political clashes in August, which left around six dead.

 

Tannery workers raise 14 demands including wage board, job security (The New Age): Tannery Workers Union (TWU), an association of tannery workers, on Tuesday urged the authorities concerned to fulfil their 14-point demand, including ensuring job security and social justice and formulation of minimum wage board for them. TWU president Abul Kalam Azad raised the demands at a coordination meeting organised by the Tannery Workers Union and Solidarity Center at a city hotel. The tannery industry s stakeholders took part in it. The other demands include actual implementation of applicable national laws and regulations maintaining international standards, establishment of legal and social justice through the practice of industrial democracy, skills-based human resource management, ensuring a neat, hygienic and safe work environment, implementation of labour welfare facilities and strengthening of non-discrimination mechanism at workplace, he told the meeting.

 

-End-
